page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-384GB is a Cloud Native family server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 64 physical cores and 64 vCPUs. The CPU operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz with a shared allocation model. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 6.0 GB of RAM per core. This configuration does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it does provide one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a clear tradeoff between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics are relatively low, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance in the bottom 10% and Geekbench single-core scores in the bottom 25%. However, the 64-core architecture delivers strong multi-threaded capabilities. Passmark CPU scores, extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests all rank in the top 25%. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also performs in the top 25% at 400.83 GB/sec. Memory performance is highlighted by a strong cached read-only small block bandwidth of 3728.41 GB/sec, while uncached large block read and write speeds remain in the middle 50%.

Given the shared CPU allocation and the contrast between weak single-core performance and strong multi-core execution, this server is suited for highly parallelized workloads that can leverage the high core count without requiring dedicated, sustained single-core CPU performance. Appropriate workloads include multi-threaded data decompression, parallel software compilation, and general-purpose database operations. The high memory capacity of 384.0 GB supports memory-intensive tasks, though the lack of local storage requires external storage integration. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU model offers a high density of cores and memory at a lower tier than dedicated-core instances, making it a viable option for resource-dense, non-real-time parallel processing.
